text: The ordered field $\mathbb{R}$ can be characterized up to isomorphism by its first-order theory.
explanation: FALSE. By the upward Lowenheim-Skolem theorem, $\mathrm{Th}(\mathbb{R})$ has models of every cardinality $\geq |\mathbb{R}|$, so no first-order theory pins $\mathbb{R}$ down up to isomorphism; only the second-order completeness axiom does. Indeed the nonstandard reals ${}^*\mathbb{R} \equiv \mathbb{R}$ are elementarily equivalent yet non-isomorphic.
